body.en: Data analysis and probability on the EST II go beyond basic means and medians to include distributions, graphical representations, and counting methods.
In how many ways can 3 students be chosen from a group of 8? \[ \binom{8}{3}=\frac{8!}{3!\cdot 5!}=\frac{8\times7\times6}{6}=56. \]

Permutations (order matters): \(^nP_r = \dfrac{n!}{(n-r)!}\). Combinations (order irrelevant): \(^nC_r = \dfrac{n!}{r!(n-r)!}\). Conditional probability: \(P(A|B) = \dfrac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}\). Independent events: \(P(A \cap B) = P(A) \cdot P(B)\). Normal distribution: ~68% within \(1\sigma\), ~95% within \(2\sigma\).

From 4 boys and 5 girls, choose a team of 4 with at least 2 girls. How many ways?

Exactly 2G: \(\binom{5}{2}\binom{4}{2}=10 \times 6=60\). Exactly 3G: \(\binom{5}{3}\binom{4}{1}=10 \times 4=40\). Exactly 4G: \(\binom{5}{4}\binom{4}{0}=5\). Total: \(105\).

caption.en: Normal distribution with mean \(\mu = 100\) and standard deviation \(\sigma = 15\). Approximately 68.2% of data falls within \([85, 115]\) (shaded), 95.4% within \([70, 130]\), and 99.7% within \([55, 145]\).

label.en: ▲ EST II Math Traps & Pitfalls — Statistics & Counting Methods

body.en:
• Permutation vs. Combination: If order or role assignment matters (e.g. President/VP/Treasurer, race positions, arrangements in a line), use permutations \(_nP_r = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!}\). If selection order does not distinguish groups (e.g. committees, hand of cards, team rosters), use combinations \(\binom{n}{r} = \frac{n!}{r!(n-r)!}\).
  • Mutually Exclusive vs. Independent Events: Two events cannot be both mutually exclusive and independent (unless one has probability 0)! Mutually exclusive means \(P(A \cap B) = 0\), so \(P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B)\). Independent means \(P(A \cap B) = P(A) \cdot P(B)\).
  • Conditional Probability Denominator: In \(P(A|B) = \frac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}\), the conditioning event \(B\) becomes the new, restricted sample space in the denominator. Never divide by \(P(A)\) when conditioning on \(B\).
  • Standard Deviation vs. Variance: Variance is \(\sigma^2\) (squared units), while standard deviation is \(\sigma = \sqrt{\text{variance}}\) (original units). Standard deviation measures dispersion: adding a constant to all data values leaves \(\sigma\) unchanged, while multiplying by \(c\) multiplies \(\sigma\) by \(|c|\).

question.en: Events \(A\) and \(B\) are such that \(P(A)=0.6\), \(P(B)=0.5\), \(P(A|B)=0.4\). Find \(P(A \cup B)\).

A committee of 5 is to be formed from 6 men and 8 women. (a) In how many ways can the committee be formed if it must contain exactly 3 women? (b) What is the probability that the committee contains at least 4 women?

solution.en:
(a) Exactly 3 women: We must choose 3 women from 8 and 2 men from 6: \[ \binom{8}{3} \times \binom{6}{2} = 56 \times 15 = 840\text{ ways}. \]

(b) Probability of at least 4 women:

  • Total ways to form any 5-member committee from 14 people: \[ \binom{14}{5} = \dfrac{14 \times 13 \times 12 \times 11 \times 10}{5 \times 4 \times 3 \times 2 \times 1} = 2002. \]
  • Exactly 4 women (4W, 1M): \(\binom{8}{4}\binom{6}{1} = 70 \times 6 = 420\).
  • Exactly 5 women (5W, 0M): \(\binom{8}{5}\binom{6}{0} = 56 \times 1 = 56\).
  • Favorable outcomes: \(420 + 56 = 476\).
  • Probability: \[ P(\text{at least 4 women}) = \dfrac{476}{2002} = \dfrac{34}{143} \approx 0.2377\, (23.8\%). \]
